content.text: The wave equation connects three fundamental properties of waves: speed, frequency, and wavelength. This simple but powerful equation allows us to calculate any one of these properties if we know the other two, making it essential for understanding all types of waves.
This equation applies to ALL types of waves: sound, light, water, seismic, and more.
The wave equation v = fλ applies to every type of wave. If you know any two of speed, frequency, and wavelength, you can always calculate the third.

Always convert units before substituting into the wave equation. For example, MHz must be converted to Hz (multiply by 10⁶) and nm must be converted to m (multiply by 10⁻⁹).

When a wave enters a new medium, its frequency stays the same (set by the source), but its speed and wavelength change. If the wave slows down, its wavelength decreases proportionally.

— Wave speed depends on the medium, not frequency. Increasing frequency decreases wavelength (at constant speed).
"All waves travel at the same speed"
— Different types of waves have very different speeds. Even the same type of wave travels at different speeds in different media.
— If speed is constant, they're inversely related. If one increases, the other decreases.
— Light travels much faster (3 × 10⁸ m/s vs ~340 m/s for sound in air). This is why we see lightning before hearing thunder.
"The wave equation only works for some waves"
— v = fλ applies to ALL waves, regardless of type.
